title: "kx patch"

description: "Patch an indexed resource with a strategic merge, JSON merge, or JSON patch."

---

Patches one indexed resource via kubectl patch. The patch itself is kubectl's: -p gives it inline, --patch-file reads it from a file, and --type picks strategic (the default), merge or json.

kubectl's other flags pass through too — --dry-run to preview the change, -o to print the patched object, --subresource to patch status or scale.

A flag kx doesn't know is refused; put it after `--` to pass it through to kubectl.

## Usage

```text
kx patch [OPTIONS] <index> [kubectl flags]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<index>` | Row number from the current listing, @name for a mark, or kind/name such as deploy/api |

## Options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run[=string]` | client or server to preview the change without making it, as kubectl takes it; kx's line says nothing was changed |
| `-o, --output string` | Output format, as kubectl takes it; kubectl's output is printed, and kx's own lines go to stderr |

## Passthrough options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--allow-missing-template-keys` | If true, ignore any errors in templates when a field or map key is missing in the template. Only applies to golang and jsonpath output formats. |
| `--field-manager string` | Name of the manager used to track field ownership. |
| `-f, --filename strings` | Filename, directory, or URL to files identifying the resource to update |
| `-k, --kustomize string` | Process the kustomization directory. This flag can't be used together with -f or -R. |
| `--local` | If true, patch will operate on the content of the file, not the server-side resource. |
| `-p, --patch string` | The patch to be applied to the resource JSON file. |
| `--patch-file string` | A file containing a patch to be applied to the resource. |
| `-R, --recursive` | Process the directory used in -f, --filename recursively. Useful when you want to manage related manifests organized within the same directory. |
| `--show-managed-fields` | If true, keep the managedFields when printing objects in JSON or YAML format. |
| `--subresource string` | If specified, patch will operate on the subresource of the requested object. |
| `--template string` | Template string or path to template file to use when -o=go-template, -o=go-template-file. The template format is golang templates [http://golang.org/pkg/text/template/#pkg-overview]. |
| `--type string` | The type of patch being provided; one of [json merge strategic] |
| `…` | kubectl's global flags too: `--context`, `--kubeconfig`, `--as` and the rest; `kubectl options` lists them |

## Global options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--no-color` | Disable styled output |
| `-h, --help` | Show this message and exit |

## Examples

```bash
kx patch 1 -p '{"spec":{"replicas":2}}'
kx patch 1 --type merge -p '{"metadata":{"labels":{"tier":"web"}}}'
kx patch 1 --type json -p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/paused"}]'
kx patch deploy/api --patch-file fix.yaml -n prod --dry-run=server
```
